column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: God creates the heavens and the earth in six days, by his word, and everything he makes is good. On the sixth day he makes man and woman in his own image to care for the world.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: God rests on the seventh day. A closer look at the making of Adam from the dust, the garden of Eden, and the first marriage, when God makes Eve and brings her to Adam.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: The serpent tempts Eve, and she and Adam eat the forbidden fruit. Sin brings shame, pain and death, but God promises that a son of the woman will crush the serpent's head.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: Cain kills his brother Abel out of jealousy and is sent away. Sin spreads through Cain's family, while Adam and Eve have another son, Seth, and people begin to call on the LORD.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: The family line from Adam to Noah, with their long lives and the refrain "and he died". Enoch is different: he walked with God, and God took him.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: The earth is full of violence and God grieves that he made mankind. But Noah finds favour, and God tells him to build an ark to save his family and the animals.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: Noah, his family and the animals go into the ark, and God shuts them in. The rain falls for forty days, and the flood covers the earth.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: The waters go down and the ark rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends out birds, leaves the ark and offers a sacrifice, and God promises never again to curse the ground.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: God blesses Noah and makes a covenant never to destroy the earth by flood, with the rainbow as its sign. Noah gets drunk, and Ham dishonours him.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: The nations that came from Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, spreading over the earth after the flood.

column4: Beginnings: creation, the fall and the flood, before Abraham
column5: People build a tower at Babel to make a name for themselves, and God confuses their language and scatters them. The line of Shem leads to Abram.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: God calls Abram to leave his homeland and promises to make him a great nation and to bless all nations through him. Abram goes to Canaan, then to Egypt in a famine.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Abram and his nephew Lot part ways because their flocks are too large. Lot chooses the land near Sodom, and God promises all the land to Abram's children.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Abram rescues Lot after raiding kings carry him off. The priest-king Melchizedek blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: God promises Abram a son and children as many as the stars, and Abram believes him; it is counted to him as righteousness. God seals the promise with a covenant.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram, and Hagar conceives. She runs away, and the LORD finds her in the desert and promises a son, Ishmael.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: God makes his covenant with Abram again, renames him Abraham and Sarai Sarah, and gives circumcision as its sign. He promises Sarah will bear a son, Isaac.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Three visitors come to Abraham, and the LORD repeats that Sarah will have a son; Sarah laughs. Abraham pleads with God for the city of Sodom.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Two angels rescue Lot and his daughters before God destroys Sodom and Gomorrah. Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Abraham again says Sarah is his sister, this time to King Abimelech of Gerar. God warns Abimelech in a dream and keeps Sarah safe.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Isaac is born, as God promised. Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, and God cares for them in the desert. Abraham makes a treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: God tests Abraham by asking him to offer Isaac. Abraham obeys, and God stops him and provides a ram in Isaac's place, renewing his promise to bless all nations.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Sarah dies, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah at Hebron to bury her, his first piece of the promised land.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Abraham's servant travels to find a wife for Isaac among his relatives. God guides him to Rebekah, who agrees to go and marry Isaac.

column4: The patriarchs: Abraham, about 2000 BC
column5: Abraham dies. Rebekah has twins, Esau and Jacob, and God says the older will serve the younger. Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a meal.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: God repeats his promises to Isaac. Isaac lives among the Philistines, digs wells, and makes peace with Abimelech.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Jacob, helped by his mother Rebekah, tricks his blind father Isaac into giving him Esau's blessing. Esau plans to kill him.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Jacob flees to his uncle Laban. At Bethel he dreams of a stairway to heaven, and God promises to be with him and bring him back.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Jacob works for Laban seven years to marry Rachel, but Laban tricks him into marrying Leah first. Leah has sons while Rachel has none.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Rachel and Leah compete for Jacob's love through their children and their servants. Rachel at last has Joseph, and Jacob's flocks grow rich.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: God tells Jacob to go home. He leaves secretly with his family and flocks, Laban chases him, and they part with a covenant.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Jacob prepares to meet Esau in fear. At night he wrestles with God, who renames him Israel.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Esau runs to meet Jacob and embraces him, and the brothers are reconciled. Jacob settles near Shechem.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: Shechem defiles Jacob's daughter Dinah. Her brothers Simeon and Levi take revenge by killing the men of the city.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: God sends Jacob back to Bethel and confirms his new name and the promises. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies.

column4: The patriarchs: Isaac and Jacob, about 1900 BC
column5: The family of Esau, who settled in Edom, and the chiefs and kings of the Edomites.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Jacob loves Joseph most and gives him a fine robe. Joseph dreams of ruling his brothers, and in jealousy they sell him as a slave to Egypt.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Judah wrongs his daughter-in-law Tamar, who tricks him to gain the children she is owed. Judah admits she was more righteous than he.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph serves Potiphar faithfully and the LORD is with him. He refuses Potiphar's wife, who lies about him, and he is put in prison.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: In prison Joseph explains the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker. It happens as he said, but the cupbearer forgets him.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph explains Pharaoh's dreams of seven good years and seven years of famine. Pharaoh puts him in charge of all Egypt to prepare.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt to buy grain and bow before him without knowing him. He tests them and keeps Simeon until they bring Benjamin.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: The brothers return with Benjamin. Joseph is moved to tears and holds a feast for them.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph hides his cup in Benjamin's sack to test his brothers. Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin's place.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph tells his brothers who he is and forgives them, seeing that God sent him ahead to save lives. He sends for his father.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: God tells Jacob not to be afraid to go down to Egypt. Jacob and all his family travel there and he sees Joseph again.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Jacob's family settles in Goshen and Jacob blesses Pharaoh. Joseph manages Egypt through the famine.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Jacob blesses Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, putting the younger first.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Jacob blesses his twelve sons before he dies, saying the sceptre will not depart from Judah. He asks to be buried in Canaan.

column4: The patriarchs: Joseph in Egypt, about 1900–1800 BC
column5: Joseph buries Jacob in Canaan and reassures his brothers: what they meant for evil, God meant for good. Joseph dies, sure that God will bring Israel home.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: A new Pharaoh fears the growing Israelites and makes them slaves. When they keep growing, he orders their baby boys killed, but the midwives fear God.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses is born and hidden in a basket, then raised by Pharaoh's daughter. He kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian and marries. God hears Israel's groaning.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: God speaks to Moses from a burning bush and sends him to free Israel. He reveals his name: "I AM WHO I AM."

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses makes excuses, and God gives him signs and his brother Aaron to speak for him. Moses returns to Egypt, and the people believe.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let the people go, and Pharaoh refuses and makes their work harder. The people blame Moses.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: God promises to bring Israel out with power and make them his people. The family line of Moses and Aaron.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Aaron's staff becomes a snake, and the first plague turns the Nile to blood. Pharaoh's heart is hard.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: The plagues of frogs, gnats and flies. Pharaoh promises to let the people go, then changes his mind.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: The plagues of disease on the livestock, boils and hail. God says he raised Pharaoh up to show his power in all the earth.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: The plagues of locusts and darkness. Pharaoh still refuses and drives Moses out.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses warns of the last plague: the death of every firstborn in Egypt.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: God gives the Passover: each family kills a lamb and puts its blood on the doorposts so the LORD passes over them. The firstborn of Egypt die, and Israel leaves.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: The firstborn are to be set apart to the LORD. God leads his people by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Pharaoh chases Israel to the Red Sea. God parts the sea, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the Egyptian army drowns.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses and Israel sing praise to the LORD for his victory. At Marah God makes bitter water sweet.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: The people grumble for food, and God sends quail and manna from heaven each morning, with a double portion before the Sabbath.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: God gives water from the rock at Horeb. Israel defeats the Amalekites while Moses holds up his hands.

column4: Out of Egypt, about 1446 BC
column5: Moses' father-in-law Jethro visits and advises him to appoint leaders to help judge the people.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Israel camps at Mount Sinai. God offers to make them his treasured people, and comes down on the mountain in fire and thunder.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: God gives the Ten Commandments. The people are afraid, and Moses draws near to God.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Laws for Hebrew servants and for injuries and violence, including "eye for eye".

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Laws about property, care for the weak, and holiness.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Laws about justice, the Sabbath year and the three yearly feasts. God promises to send his angel ahead of them.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The people promise to obey, and the covenant is sealed with blood. Moses goes up the mountain for forty days.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: God gives the plans for the tabernacle, so he may live among his people: the ark, the table and the lampstand.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Plans for the tabernacle's curtains, frames and the veil before the Most Holy Place.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Plans for the bronze altar, the courtyard and oil for the lamp.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The holy garments for Aaron and his sons, the priests, with the names of Israel's tribes on the high priest's breastpiece.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: How the priests are to be set apart, and the daily offerings. God will dwell among Israel and be their God.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The altar of incense, the atonement money, the bronze basin, the anointing oil and incense.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: God fills Bezalel with his Spirit to build the tabernacle. The Sabbath is a sign between God and Israel. God gives the two tablets.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: While Moses is on the mountain the people make a golden calf. Moses breaks the tablets and pleads with God for the people.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: God says he will not go with the people, then agrees when Moses pleads. Moses asks to see his glory.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: God gives new tablets and proclaims his name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger. Moses' face shines.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Moses gathers the people's willing gifts for the tabernacle.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The people bring more than enough, and the skilled workers make the curtains and frames.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: Bezalel makes the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altar of incense.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: They make the altar of burnt offering, the basin and the courtyard. An account of the metals used.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The priests' garments are made, and the finished work is brought to Moses, who blesses the people.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1446–1445 BC
column5: The tabernacle is set up, and the glory of the LORD fills it. The cloud leads Israel on their journeys.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How to bring a burnt offering: an animal without defect, wholly burned, given for acceptance before God.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How to bring a grain offering of flour, oil and incense, a gift of thanks to the LORD.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How to bring a peace offering, a shared meal of fellowship with God.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The sin offering for those who sin without meaning to: priests, the whole people, leaders and ordinary people.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The guilt offering: confessing sin and making things right, with a gift for those who are poor.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: More instructions for the priests about the offerings and the fire on the altar that must never go out.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The priests' share of the offerings and the rules for the peace offerings.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Moses ordains Aaron and his sons as priests with washing, garments, anointing and sacrifice.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Aaron offers the first sacrifices, and fire comes from the LORD and consumes the offering. The people shout and fall on their faces.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorised fire and die. God must be treated as holy.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Which animals are clean and may be eaten, and which are unclean. "Be holy, for I am holy."

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How a mother is made clean again after giving birth.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How the priest is to examine skin diseases and mould on clothing.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How a person healed of a skin disease is cleansed, and what to do about mould in a house.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Uncleanness from bodily discharges, and how to be made clean.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The Day of Atonement: the high priest enters the Most Holy Place with blood, and the scapegoat carries the people's sins away.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Sacrifices must be brought to the tabernacle, and blood must not be eaten, for the life is in the blood.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: God forbids the sexual sins of Egypt and Canaan; his people are to live by his ways.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Laws for holy living in everyday life: honour parents, care for the poor and the foreigner, and love your neighbour as yourself.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Punishments for idolatry, for sins against family and for sexual sins. Israel is set apart to be God's own.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Rules of holiness for the priests and the high priest.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: How priests must handle the holy offerings, and offerings must be without defect.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The yearly feasts: Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The lamp and the holy bread. A man who blasphemes God's name is put to death.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: The Sabbath year and the Year of Jubilee, when land returns to its families and slaves are freed.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Blessings if Israel obeys and curses if they rebel, with God's promise to remember his covenant when they repent.

column4: At Mount Sinai: laws for worship and holy living, about 1445 BC
column5: Rules for vows and for things given to the LORD, including the tithe.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: Moses counts the fighting men of each tribe. The Levites are set apart to care for the tabernacle.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: How the tribes camp around the tabernacle and march in order.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The Levites are counted and given to the LORD in place of Israel's firstborn.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The duties of the Levite clans in carrying the tabernacle.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: Unclean people are kept outside the camp; wrongs must be confessed and repaid; the test for a wife suspected of unfaithfulness.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The Nazirite vow, and the priestly blessing: "The LORD bless you and keep you."

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The leaders of the tribes bring gifts to dedicate the altar.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The lampstand is set up, and the Levites are cleansed and set apart.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: The second Passover. The cloud over the tabernacle shows Israel when to move and when to stay.

column4: At Mount Sinai, about 1445 BC
column5: Silver trumpets are made. Israel leaves Sinai, following the ark.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: The people complain about the manna and crave meat. God gives seventy elders his Spirit, and sends quail with a plague.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses, and God defends Moses, his faithful servant. Miriam is struck with a skin disease.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: Twelve spies explore Canaan. Ten say the people are too strong, but Caleb says they can take it.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: The people refuse to enter Canaan. God says that generation will die in the wilderness; only Caleb and Joshua will enter.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: More laws for offerings, and tassels on clothing to remind Israel of God's commands.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel against Moses and Aaron, and the ground swallows them.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: Aaron's staff buds, showing God has chosen him as priest.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: The duties and share of the priests and Levites.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: The ashes of a red heifer are used to cleanse those made unclean by a dead body.

column4: In the wilderness: forty years of wandering, about 1445–1407 BC
column5: Miriam dies. Moses strikes the rock in anger instead of speaking to it, and may not enter Canaan. Aaron dies.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Israel complains, and God sends snakes; those who look at the bronze snake live. Israel defeats Sihon and Og.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: King Balak of Moab hires Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the LORD.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Balaam tries to curse Israel but can only bless them, for God is not a man that he should lie.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Balaam blesses Israel again and foretells a star rising from Jacob.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Israel joins in Moab's idol worship and sexual sin. Phinehas stops the plague with his zeal.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: A second census of the new generation before entering Canaan.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: The daughters of Zelophehad receive their father's land. Joshua is chosen to lead after Moses.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: The daily, Sabbath, monthly and Passover offerings.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: The offerings for the autumn feasts.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Rules for vows made by men and by women.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Israel takes vengeance on Midian.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: The tribes of Reuben and Gad, and half of Manasseh, settle east of the Jordan, promising to help conquer Canaan.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: A list of Israel's journeys from Egypt to the plains of Moab.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: The borders of the promised land and the leaders who will divide it.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Towns for the Levites and cities of refuge for those who kill someone by accident.

column4: On the plains of Moab, about 1407 BC
column5: Women who inherit land must marry within their tribe, so each tribe keeps its land.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Moses reminds the new generation how their parents refused to enter the land from Kadesh.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Moses recalls the years of wandering and the victory over Sihon.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Moses recalls the defeat of Og and the land east of the Jordan. God lets him see the land but not enter it.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Moses urges Israel to obey God and not make idols, for there is no other god. If they seek him, they will find him.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Moses repeats the Ten Commandments given at Sinai.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Hear, O Israel: love the LORD your God with all your heart, and teach his words to your children.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Israel must destroy the idols of Canaan, for God chose them out of his love, not because they were great.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: God humbled Israel in the desert to teach that man does not live by bread alone. Do not forget him when you are rich.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Israel will win the land not because they are righteous; Moses recalls the golden calf.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: God gives new tablets. What does the LORD require? To fear him, walk in his ways and love him.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: The blessings of obedience; keep God's words on your hearts and teach them to your children.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Israel is to worship only at the place God chooses, not at the pagan high places.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: How to deal with false prophets and anyone who leads others to idols.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Clean and unclean food, and the tithe.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Debts are cancelled every seventh year; be generous to the poor and free Hebrew slaves.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Passover, the Feast of Weeks and the Feast of Tabernacles; judges must be fair.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Laws for courts, and for a future king, who must read God's law all his life.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: The priests' share; detestable practices forbidden; God will raise up a prophet like Moses.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Cities of refuge, boundary stones and honest witnesses.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Rules for war, trusting in the LORD who fights for Israel.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Unsolved murders, captive wives, the rights of the firstborn and a rebellious son.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Various laws about neighbours, kindness to animals and sexual purity.

column4: Moses' last words on the plains of Moab, about 1406 BC
column5: Who may enter the assembly, cleanliness in the camp and honesty in vows.

column4: Psalms, Book 2: songs of the sons of Korah, Asaph and David
column5: A short urgent cry: hurry to help me, O God.

column4: Psalms, Book 2: songs of the sons of Korah, Asaph and David
column5: An old person's prayer: you have been my hope since my youth.

column4: Psalms, Book 2: songs of the sons of Korah, Asaph and David
column5: A prayer for the king's righteous reign, which will reach to the ends of the earth.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Asaph envies the prosperous wicked until he enters God's sanctuary and sees their end. God is my strength for ever.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: A lament after the enemy destroyed the temple: remember your people.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: God is the judge: he brings one down and lifts up another.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: God is known in Judah and breaks the weapons of war.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: In trouble, the psalmist remembers God's mighty deeds, like leading Israel through the sea.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: A history lesson: Israel's forgetfulness and God's patience, from Egypt to David.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: A lament over Jerusalem's ruin: help us for the glory of your name.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Restore us, O God; let your face shine. Israel is a vine God planted.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Sing to God; if only my people would listen to me.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: God judges the unjust rulers and calls them to defend the weak.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: A prayer against nations plotting against Israel, that they may know the LORD is Most High.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: How lovely is your dwelling place: a day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Revive us again; love and faithfulness meet together.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Teach me your way, O LORD; unite my heart to fear your name.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: Glorious things are spoken of Zion, birthplace of people from every nation.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: The darkest psalm: a cry from deep despair, still addressed to the God who saves.

column4: Psalms, Book 3: songs of Asaph and others, some from the time of the exile
column5: God's covenant with David and his faithfulness, yet a lament that the king has fallen.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Moses' prayer: God is eternal, our lives are short; teach us to number our days.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High is safe under his wings.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: It is good to give thanks to the LORD; the righteous flourish like a palm tree.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: The LORD reigns, robed in majesty; his throne is established from of old.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: The God who avenges will judge the proud; his comfort cheers my soul.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Come, let us worship and bow down before our Maker; do not harden your hearts.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Sing to the LORD a new song; tell his glory among the nations.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice; he guards the lives of his faithful.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Make a joyful noise to the LORD, the King, who has made known his salvation.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: The LORD our God is holy; exalt him.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Enter his gates with thanksgiving; the LORD is good and his love endures for ever.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: David promises to lead a blameless life and keep evil out of his house.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: A prayer of the afflicted: my days fade, but you remain the same for ever.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits; as far as the east is from the west he removes our sins.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Praise to God the Creator, who cares for every living thing.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Give thanks to the LORD for his faithfulness to Abraham, Joseph and Israel in Egypt.

column4: Psalms, Book 4: from Moses' prayer to songs of God's kingship
column5: Israel's long history of sin and God's mercy again and again.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Give thanks: God rescued the lost, the prisoners, the sick and those at sea when they cried to him.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Be exalted, O God; with God we will gain the victory.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: David prays against cruel accusers and trusts God's steadfast love.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: The LORD says to my Lord: sit at my right hand. A priest for ever like Melchizedek.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Praise for God's great works; the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Blessed is the one who fears the LORD; he is generous and not afraid of bad news.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Praise the LORD, who stoops down to lift the needy from the dust.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: When Israel came out of Egypt, the sea fled and the mountains skipped.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Not to us, O LORD, but to your name give glory; idols are lifeless.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: I love the LORD, for he heard my voice and saved me from death.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: The shortest psalm: praise the LORD, all nations, for his love is great.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Give thanks, his love endures for ever. The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: The longest psalm, in 22 sections for the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, delighting in God's word: a lamp to my feet.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: In my distress I cried to the LORD; I long for peace among those who hate it.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: I lift my eyes to the hills: my help comes from the LORD, who never sleeps.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Joy at going up to the house of the LORD; pray for the peace of Jerusalem.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: We look to the LORD for mercy, as a servant looks to his master.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: If the LORD had not been on our side, we would have been swallowed up.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Those who trust the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: When God restored Zion we were like dreamers; those who sow in tears will reap with joy.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Unless the LORD builds the house, they labour in vain; children are a gift from him.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: The blessings of the one who fears the LORD and walks in his ways.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Israel has been afflicted often, but its enemies have not prevailed.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Out of the depths I cry to you; with you there is forgiveness; I wait for the LORD.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: I have calmed and quieted my soul like a weaned child with its mother.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: A prayer for David's line and for God's dwelling in Zion.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: A call to bless the LORD in his house by night.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Praise the LORD, who chose Israel and is greater than all idols.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love endures for ever, the refrain after every line.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: By the rivers of Babylon the exiles weep when they remember Zion.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Thanks with my whole heart: the LORD will fulfil his purpose for me.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: God knows me completely and is everywhere; I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Search me, O God.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: A prayer for rescue from violent and evil men.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Set a guard over my mouth; keep me from evil.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: From a cave, David cries out: you are my refuge.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: A prayer for mercy and guidance: teach me to do your will.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Blessed be the LORD my rock, who trains my hands for war; blessed are the people whose God is the LORD.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; he is gracious and near to all who call on him.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Do not trust in princes; blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Praise God, who heals the brokenhearted and counts the stars.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Let all creation praise the LORD: angels, sun, moon, sea creatures and people.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Sing a new song; the LORD takes pleasure in his people.

column4: Psalms, Book 5: songs of thanks, ascent and praise, many from after the exile
column5: Praise him with every instrument; let everything that has breath praise the LORD.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Why the proverbs were written. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; do not follow sinners. Wisdom calls out in the streets.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Seek wisdom like hidden treasure, for the LORD gives wisdom, and it will keep you from evil.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Trust in the LORD with all your heart and do not lean on your own understanding; he will make your paths straight.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: A father urges his son to get wisdom; guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: A warning against adultery; enjoy the wife of your youth.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Warnings against laziness (go to the ant), deceit, and seven things the LORD hates.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: A young man is led astray by an adulterous woman; do not let your heart turn to her ways.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Wisdom speaks: she was with God at creation, and whoever finds her finds life.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's teaching to his son, about 950 BC
column5: Wisdom and Folly both invite people to their houses; the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Short sayings contrasting the wise and the foolish, the righteous and the wicked.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about honesty, pride, generosity and the righteous.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about the tongue, hard work and listening to advice.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about discipline, wealth and good company: walk with the wise and become wise.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about wise living; there is a way that seems right, but its end is death.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: A gentle answer turns away wrath; sayings about words, the heart and the LORD's care.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: People plan their way, but the LORD directs their steps. Pride goes before destruction.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about peace, friendship and foolishness: a friend loves at all times.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; sayings about words and relationships.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about poverty, patience and God's purposes, which stand.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: Sayings about wine, honesty, kings and trusting God to guide our steps.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: The king's heart is in the LORD's hand; sayings about justice and pride.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: A good name is better than riches; train up a child in the way he should go.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: The sayings of the wise: on greed, discipline and the dangers of drink.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's short sayings and the sayings of the wise
column5: More sayings of the wise: do not envy the wicked; the righteous rise again.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: Hezekiah's collection: humility before the king, and kindness to enemies.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: Sayings about fools, the lazy and gossip.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: Sayings about friendship and planning: as iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: Sayings about righteousness and confession: whoever confesses sin finds mercy.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: Sayings about discipline, leaders and trust in the LORD.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: The words of Agur: every word of God proves true; he is a shield.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's sayings copied by Hezekiah's men, about 700 BC, and the words of Agur and Lemuel
column5: King Lemuel's mother's advice, and the poem of the wife of noble character who fears the LORD.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: The Preacher says everything under the sun is vanity, a fleeting breath; nothing is new.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: He tried pleasure, great projects and wealth, and found them empty without God.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: There is a time for everything; God has set eternity in our hearts.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Oppression, envy and loneliness; two are better than one.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Be careful when you come before God, and do not love money.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Riches cannot satisfy; who knows what is good for a person?

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Wise sayings about sorrow, patience and the limits of wisdom.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Obey the king; it will go well with those who fear God, though life is hard to understand.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Everyone dies; so enjoy life with those you love and work with all your might.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Wisdom and folly in leaders and in everyday work.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Cast your bread on the waters; enjoy your youth, but remember God will judge.

column4: Wisdom: the Preacher (traditionally Solomon) on the meaning of life, about 935 BC
column5: Remember your Creator in your youth. The end of the matter: fear God and keep his commandments.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The bride longs for her beloved, the king, and they praise each other.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The lovers delight in each other; the beloved calls her to come away with him in springtime.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The bride searches for her love at night; Solomon's wedding procession.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The bridegroom praises the beauty of his bride.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The bride is slow to open, her beloved leaves, and she searches for him, describing his beauty.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The lovers are reunited: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: The bridegroom delights in his bride, and she gives herself to him.

column4: Wisdom: Solomon's song of love, about 950 BC
column5: Love is as strong as death; many waters cannot quench it.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: God charges Judah with rebellion and empty worship; come, though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: In the last days all nations will come to God's mountain, and swords will be beaten into ploughshares.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Judah's leaders and proud women will face judgment.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: After judgment, the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and Zion will be holy.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The song of the vineyard: God's people produced bad fruit. Woe to the greedy and the proud.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Isaiah sees the LORD on his throne, is cleansed, and answers: Here am I, send me.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: King Ahaz will not trust God; the sign: a virgin will conceive and bear a son, Immanuel.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Assyria is coming; fear the LORD, who is a sanctuary to those who trust him.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A light dawns: a child is born, Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Assyria is the rod of God's anger, but will itself be judged; a remnant will return.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A shoot from Jesse's stump: the Spirit-filled King will bring justice and peace, and the wolf will live with the lamb.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A song of praise: God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A prophecy against Babylon: the day of the LORD is coming.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The proud king of Babylon falls like the morning star; God's purpose against Assyria stands.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A lament over the destruction of Moab.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Moab's fall; a throne will be set up in love in David's house.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A prophecy against Damascus and Israel, who forgot the God of their salvation.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A message to Cush: gifts will be brought to the LORD on Mount Zion.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Egypt will be struck, but will turn to the LORD; Egypt and Assyria will worship with Israel.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign that Egypt and Cush will be taken captive.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Babylon has fallen; prophecies against Edom and Arabia.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Jerusalem's leaders feast instead of repenting; the key of David is given to Eliakim.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A prophecy against Tyre, the proud trading city.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The LORD will judge the whole earth and reign on Mount Zion.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: God will prepare a feast for all peoples and swallow up death for ever.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A song of trust: you keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is fixed on you.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: God will care for his vineyard and gather his people.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Judgment on Ephraim's drunken leaders; God lays in Zion a precious cornerstone.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: People honour God with their lips, but their hearts are far from him.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Do not trust Egypt; in returning and rest you shall be saved, in quietness and trust is your strength.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Woe to those who rely on Egypt's horses instead of the Holy One of Israel.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: A king will reign in righteousness; the Spirit will be poured out.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The LORD is our judge, our lawgiver, our king; he will save us.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: God's judgment on the nations and on Edom.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The desert will bloom; the blind will see and the lame will leap, as the redeemed return to Zion.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: The Assyrian commander mocks Hezekiah and the LORD outside Jerusalem.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Hezekiah prays, and the angel of the LORD strikes down the Assyrian army.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Hezekiah is sick and prays; God adds fifteen years to his life.

column4: Isaiah prophesies to Judah before and during the Assyrian threat, about 740–700 BC
column5: Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylon's envoys, and Isaiah foretells exile to Babylon.

column4: Comfort for God's people, looking ahead to the return from Babylon and the Servant
column5: Comfort my people. Prepare the way of the LORD; those who wait on the LORD will renew their strength.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: The example of the Macedonians' giving; Christ became poor so you might become rich.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: God loves a cheerful giver; he is able to make all grace abound.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: Paul defends his ministry: take every thought captive to Christ.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: Paul answers the false apostles by boasting of his sufferings.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: Paul's thorn in the flesh: my grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Corinth, about AD 56
column5: Examine yourselves; Paul's final warnings and blessing.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: Paul is astonished that the Galatians are turning to a different gospel; his gospel came from Christ.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: Paul confronts Peter; we are justified by faith in Christ, not works of the law. I have been crucified with Christ.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: Did you receive the Spirit by the law or by faith? The righteous shall live by faith; all are one in Christ.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: You are no longer slaves but sons and heirs; Hagar and Sarah as two covenants.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: Stand firm in freedom. Walk by the Spirit; the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.

column4: Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia, about AD 48–49
column5: Bear one another's burdens; you reap what you sow; boast only in the cross.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Every spiritual blessing in Christ: chosen, redeemed, forgiven and sealed with the Spirit. Paul prays for them.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Dead in sin, made alive by grace through faith; Jews and Gentiles are one new people in Christ.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: The mystery revealed: Gentiles share in the promise. Paul prays that they may know Christ's love.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Live worthy of your calling in unity; the gifts Christ gives; put off the old self, put on the new.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Imitate God and walk in love and light; wives and husbands, as the church and Christ.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Ephesus, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Children and parents, servants and masters; put on the whole armour of God.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Philippi, written from prison, about AD 61
column5: Paul thanks God for the Philippians; his chains have spread the gospel. For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Philippi, written from prison, about AD 61
column5: Have the mind of Christ, who humbled himself to death on a cross and was exalted. Timothy and Epaphroditus.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Philippi, written from prison, about AD 61
column5: Paul counts everything loss compared to knowing Christ, and presses on toward the goal.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Philippi, written from prison, about AD 61
column5: Rejoice in the Lord; do not be anxious but pray; I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Colossae, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Christ is the image of the invisible God; all things were created through him and hold together in him.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Colossae, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: In Christ the fullness of God dwells bodily; do not be taken captive by empty philosophy or rules.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Colossae, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Set your minds on things above; put on love; whatever you do, do it for the Lord.

column4: Paul's letter to the church in Colossae, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Devote yourselves to prayer; let your speech be gracious; greetings.

column4: Paul's first letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 50–51
column5: Paul thanks God for their faith, love and hope; they turned from idols to serve the living God.

column4: Paul's first letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 50–51
column5: Paul recalls his gentle care among them; they received God's word as truly God's word.

column4: Paul's first letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 50–51
column5: Timothy's good news of their faith; Paul prays for their love to increase.

column4: Paul's first letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 50–51
column5: Live to please God in holiness; the Lord will come, and the dead in Christ will rise first.

column4: Paul's first letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 50–51
column5: Be ready for the day of the Lord; rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 51
column5: God will repay those who trouble them when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 51
column5: The day of the Lord has not come yet; the man of lawlessness must come first. Stand firm.

column4: Paul's second letter to the church in Thessalonica, about AD 51
column5: Pray for us; avoid idleness: if anyone will not work, let him not eat.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Guard against false teaching; Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Pray for everyone; there is one God and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus. Worship in the church.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Qualifications for overseers and deacons; the mystery of godliness.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Beware of false teachers; train yourself in godliness; let no one despise your youth.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Caring for widows, honouring elders and correcting sin.

column4: Paul's letter to Timothy, leading the church in Ephesus, about AD 62–64
column5: Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money is a root of all evil; fight the good fight.

column4: Paul's last letter, to Timothy, from prison in Rome, about AD 67
column5: God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power, love and self-control; guard the gospel.

column4: Paul's last letter, to Timothy, from prison in Rome, about AD 67
column5: Be strong in grace; a good soldier of Christ; rightly handle the word of truth.

column4: Paul's last letter, to Timothy, from prison in Rome, about AD 67
column5: Hard times will come in the last days; all Scripture is breathed out by God and useful.

column4: Paul's last letter, to Timothy, from prison in Rome, about AD 67
column5: Preach the word; Paul has fought the good fight and finished the race.

column4: Paul's letter to Titus, leading the churches on Crete, about AD 63–65
column5: Appoint elders who are above reproach and hold firm to sound teaching.

column4: Paul's letter to Titus, leading the churches on Crete, about AD 63–65
column5: Teach sound doctrine to every age; the grace of God has appeared, training us to live godly lives.

column4: Paul's letter to Titus, leading the churches on Crete, about AD 63–65
column5: God saved us by his mercy, not by our works, through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

column4: Paul's letter to Philemon, written from prison, about AD 60–62
column5: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus, now a believer, as a dear brother.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: God has spoken by his Son, who is the radiance of his glory and is greater than the angels.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Pay attention so we do not drift away; Jesus became like us to help those who are tempted.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Jesus is greater than Moses; do not harden your hearts as Israel did in the wilderness.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: A Sabbath rest remains for God's people; the word of God is living and active; we have a high priest who sympathizes.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Jesus is high priest like Melchizedek; a warning to grow up in the faith.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Go on to maturity; God's promise is an anchor for the soul.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Jesus is a priest for ever, like Melchizedek, and always lives to intercede for us.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Jesus serves in the true tabernacle as mediator of a better, new covenant.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: The old tabernacle pointed to Christ, who entered heaven with his own blood once for all.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: By one sacrifice Christ has made perfect for ever those being made holy; hold fast and do not give up meeting together.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for: the heroes of faith from Abel to the prophets.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Run the race looking to Jesus; God disciplines those he loves; you have come to Mount Zion.

column4: A letter to Jewish Christians (author not named), before AD 70
column5: Love one another, be content, remember your leaders; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and for ever.

column4: James, the Lord's brother, writes to Jewish Christians, about AD 45–50
column5: Count trials joy, ask God for wisdom, and be doers of the word, not hearers only.

column4: James, the Lord's brother, writes to Jewish Christians, about AD 45–50
column5: Do not show favouritism; faith without works is dead.

column4: James, the Lord's brother, writes to Jewish Christians, about AD 45–50
column5: The tongue is a fire hard to tame; wisdom from above is pure and peaceable.

column4: James, the Lord's brother, writes to Jewish Christians, about AD 45–50
column5: Quarrels come from selfish desires; humble yourselves, draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.

column4: James, the Lord's brother, writes to Jewish Christians, about AD 45–50
column5: Warning to the rich; be patient; pray for one another, for the prayer of a righteous person is powerful.

column4: Peter writes to suffering Christians in Asia Minor, about AD 62–64
column5: God has given us new birth into a living hope; be holy, for you were redeemed by Christ's precious blood.

column4: Peter writes to suffering Christians in Asia Minor, about AD 62–64
column5: You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood; Christ suffered for you, leaving an example.

column4: Peter writes to suffering Christians in Asia Minor, about AD 62–64
column5: Wives and husbands; repay evil with blessing; always be ready to give a reason for your hope.

column4: Peter writes to suffering Christians in Asia Minor, about AD 62–64
column5: Do not be surprised by suffering; use your gifts to serve one another.

column4: Peter writes to suffering Christians in Asia Minor, about AD 62–64
column5: Elders, shepherd the flock; cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.

column4: Peter's last letter, shortly before his death, about AD 65–68
column5: Add goodness, knowledge and love to your faith; Scripture came from God as men were carried along by the Spirit.

column4: Peter's last letter, shortly before his death, about AD 65–68
column5: False teachers will come and be judged, but the Lord knows how to rescue the godly.

column4: Peter's last letter, shortly before his death, about AD 65–68
column5: The Lord is not slow about his promise; he is patient, wanting all to repent. The day of the Lord will come.

column4: John writes to churches he cares for, about AD 85–95
column5: We proclaim the Word of life; God is light. If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive us.

column4: John writes to churches he cares for, about AD 85–95
column5: Jesus is our advocate; whoever says he knows God must keep his commands; do not love the world.

column4: John writes to churches he cares for, about AD 85–95
column5: See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; love one another in deed.

column4: John writes to churches he cares for, about AD 85–95
column5: Test the spirits; God is love, and perfect love casts out fear.

column4: John writes to churches he cares for, about AD 85–95
column5: Faith overcomes the world; whoever has the Son has life, that you may know you have eternal life.

column4: John's short letter to "the elect lady and her children", about AD 85–95
column5: Walk in truth and love, and do not welcome those who deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh.

column4: John's short letter to his friend Gaius, about AD 85–95
column5: John praises Gaius for welcoming travelling teachers and warns against proud Diotrephes.

column4: Jude, the brother of James, warns the church, about AD 65–80
column5: Contend for the faith once for all delivered; false teachers will be judged; God is able to keep you from falling.

column4: John's vision on Patmos and the letters to seven churches, about AD 95
column5: John on Patmos sees the risen Jesus among seven lampstands: I am the Alpha and the Omega.

column4: John's vision on Patmos and the letters to seven churches, about AD 95
column5: Letters to the churches in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum and Thyatira: hold fast and overcome.

column4: John's vision on Patmos and the letters to seven churches, about AD 95
column5: Letters to Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea: I stand at the door and knock.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: A door opens in heaven: God on his throne, worshipped day and night: holy, holy, holy.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: Only the Lamb who was slain is worthy to open the scroll, and all creation praises him.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The Lamb opens six seals: conquest, war, famine, death, martyrs crying out, and a great earthquake.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: God's servants are sealed; a great multitude from every nation stands before the throne.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The seventh seal; the first four trumpets bring judgment on the earth.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The fifth and sixth trumpets bring terrible plagues, yet people do not repent.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: A mighty angel with a little scroll; John eats it and must prophesy again.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: Two witnesses prophesy, are killed and rise; the seventh trumpet: the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: A woman, her child and the dragon; war in heaven; they overcame by the blood of the Lamb.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: A beast from the sea and a beast from the earth demand worship; the mark of the beast.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The Lamb on Mount Zion; angels announce the gospel and judgment; the harvest of the earth.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The song of Moses and the Lamb; seven angels with seven last plagues.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The seven bowls of God's wrath are poured out.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The great prostitute Babylon riding the beast; the Lamb will conquer, for he is Lord of lords.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: Babylon the great has fallen, and the world mourns her.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: Heaven rejoices; the marriage supper of the Lamb; Christ rides out as King of kings and defeats the beast.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: Satan is bound for a thousand years, then defeated for ever; the dead are judged before the great white throne.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: A new heaven and a new earth; God will dwell with his people and wipe away every tear. The new Jerusalem.

column4: John's visions of heaven, judgment and the new creation
column5: The river of life and the tree of life; Jesus says, "I am coming soon." Come, Lord Jesus.
